## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@9670dc2f6a8f013c78bab1067baae2b1fab5fd45

content.text:
Simplest robust: static HTML/CSS/JS game, no deps. Need be impressive, complete playable, mobile. Need build now.

We need design a 2D card martial arts game like Martial Arts Brutality. Let's recall that game: card-based fighting, choose cards representing moves, each body part? Martial Arts Brutality is a game where you build a deck of techniques, fight opponents with body-part damage, use stances, blocks, counter, stamina, limb damage. Cards have speed, damage, effects. Campaign with progression, upgrade cards.

Let's build a polished single-page web game:

Title: "IRON LOTUS: Path of the Fist" (or "Jade Fist"). A card battler campaign.

Core concept:
- Player selects cards from hand each round simultaneously? A compelling mechanic: each turn choose one Technique card (attack/defend/utility) plus a Stance card? Or plan 3-card sequence? Martial Arts Brutality uses a timeline where cards execute. Could simulate a real-time-ish simultaneous turn. But straightforward turn-based easier.

Let's design:
- Combat is turn-based with initiative. Each fighter has 3 body zones (Head, Torso, Legs) each with HP? Maybe simpler: one HP + guard + focus/stamina and status effects. To evoke martial arts: cards have speed, damage, guard, effects, combos, and each fighter commits a card face-down; faster card strikes first, can interrupt. That's engaging.
- Player has a deck of technique cards. Each turn draws 5, energy (Chi) 3. Play cards to attack/block/apply buffs. Enemy has telegraphed intent (like Slay the Spire) but with martial arts flavor. Campaign with 8 fights across 4 chapters, 3 opponents per chapter? Make 8-10 opponents.
- Progression: earn "insight" (gold) and XP. Level up max HP/chi. Card upgrades at dojo: spend insight to upgrade cards (+damage, reduce cost, add effects); unlock new cards. Permanent progression. Save via localStorage. Map screen with nodes.
- Maybe chi spend and stance mechanics: cards have stance (Crane/Tiger/Serpent). Playing same stance card consecutively builds Flow/Combo. Could be complexity.
- Add hit reaction, screen shake, particle slash effects, silhouetted fighters drawn with CSS/SVG? Need visual quality. We can use Canvas for combat animation, with 2D vector fighters. That can look nice. Or DOM with illustrated stick-figure martial artists via SVG and animated attacks. Since no external assets, create stylized ink-brush aesthetic with CSS + canvas particles.

Could implement 2D fighter visuals using canvas: dojo background gradient, mountains, moon, bamboo, two stylized martial artist figures with limbs, animated strikes, damage numbers, impacts. Need produce polished result.

Need support mobile with touch controls, responsive layout.

Let's plan game architecture in vanilla JS modules? Static files. We can do:
- index.html
- css/style.css
- js/data.js (cards, enemies, progression)
- js/engine.js (combat logic)
- js/ui.js / main.js
- maybe audio.js using WebAudio synth (procedural sounds) - great for polish.

Could instead create Vite React project but no need; static works. But complexity of 3k lines JS manageable. Let's aim ~2000-3000 lines total.

Game spec detailed:

Title / meta:
IRON LOTUS — a hand-inked card martial arts saga.
Player "The Wanderer" begins at Bronze Bell Dojo, challenge 10 martial artists across 5 chapters, final boss "Master Kurogane".

Screens:
1. Title screen: logo, "Begin Journey"/"Continue", settings (sound toggle), how to play.
2. Campaign map: chapter tabs? A scroll map with nodes in a path, locked/unlocked, opponent portrait/name/difficulty, rewards preview. Player stats panel (level, XP, HP, insight, deck). Buttons: Deck (view/edit), Dojo (upgrade shop), Cards? 
3. Battle screen: enemy at top/right, player bottom/left, canvas stage. HP bars, stance indicator, turn counter, intent, energy, hand of cards at bottom. On play card, resolve animation/log. Enemy turn after cards/end turn.
4. Victory screen: rewards, card choice (choose 1 of 3 new cards), insight, XP. Defeat: retry/adjust deck.
5. Deck builder: view cards, remove? Upgrade in Dojo. Deck size maybe all owned cards? Could use fixed deck of 8-12. Real progression: start deck 8 cards, gain card rewards, upgrades. Option to include/exclude? Simpler: all owned cards in deck. Upgrades at Dojo. Could add deck max 12 and allow toggle? For gameplay, hand drawn from owned deck.

Card mechanics:
Stats: name, type (Strike, Guard, Technique, Stance?), cost chi 0-3, damage, block, speed? effects.
Status effects:
- Bleed: take X at turn end (stacks)
- Stagger: enemy skips? maybe "Stun" 
- Focus: increases next attack damage by 50%
- Counter: retaliate damage when hit
- Dodge: negate next attack
- Chi regen
- Weak: deal 25% less
- Vulnerable: take 25% more
- Poison? "Pressure point"
- Combo/Flow: if previous card's stance matched, bonus damage.

Stances: Tiger (aggressive), Crane (defensive/counter), Serpent (evasive/chi). Cards have stance. Each turn, if two same stance consecutively, gain Flow 1; playing card of different stance resets. Maybe too hidden. Could show "Style" indicator and bonus.

Better core: "Momentum" resource built when attacking; spend on finishers. But chi energy already.

Let's make combat smooth:
- Player starts with HP 60, Chi 3 per turn, draw 5.
- Cards cost chi. End turn discards hand and draws new. Unplayed cards return to draw pile? Slay the Spire style discard.
- Enemy intents show attack/block/buff with exact damage.
- Attack calculations with strength, vulnerable, etc.
- 3 attack types hit zones? Let's incorporate body-part damage:
  Each fighter has Head, Torso, Legs HP? But UI could be busy. Martial Arts Brutality has damaging limbs that disable moves. We can simplify to "Balance" (posture) meter: attacks build stagger; when posture broken, enemy is stunned and takes +50% damage next turn. This gives martial arts feel. Add posture bar under HP. Defend to recover posture. That is great.
  - Posture 0..100 (increases when hit). At 100, "BREAK" -> lose remaining turn? Then posture resets and take "critical" vulnerability.
  - Player posture too; if broken, skip next card? Could be harsh. Simpler stagger meter regenerates by 15 each turn and when full "Stunned", skip enemy turn; damage to player still. Enemy stun is satisfying.
- Also "Counter" stance: play guard cards.

Enemy AI:
- Intent sequence with some randomness and conditions; each enemy has deck-like moves with weights and cooldowns. Choose move each turn.
- Elite/boss mechanics.

Campaign:
Opponents with escalating HP, unique mechanics, dialogue/intro text:
Chapter 1 – The Bamboo Gate:
 1. Ren, the Eager Student (HP 32) – basic.
 2. Two-Blades Taro (HP 45) – dual strikes/bleed.
 3. Sister Mei (HP 55) – counters.

function lerpPose(a,b,t) {
 const out={}

 return out
}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D card-based martial arts campaign game with real progression and card upgrades, inspired by *Martial Arts Brutality*, starting from an empty repo.

## Requirements
- User asked: “A 2d style card martial art game, you have a campaign where you fight martial artist, real progression, you can upgrade cards, like the game Martial Arts Brutality”
- Build request explicitly says: build complete playable game, do not ask clarifying questions, make reasonable assumptions, note them briefly at finish.
- Must work on Android/iOS phones and tablets with responsive layout and touch controls.

## Decisions
- Built as a static vanilla HTML/CSS/JS site (no npm dependencies) served by existing runtime.
- Fantasy setting: **IRON LOTUS**, ten trials across four chapters.
- Core mechanics: Chi energy, hand of 5, posture/balance break, stance Flow bonus, Bleed/Vulnerable/Weak/Strength/Counter/Dodge/Focus statuses.
- Progression: XP/levels, max HP/Chi growth, insight currency, Dojo card tempering (3 levels), post-battle card reward choice, persistent localStorage save.
- Visual direction: dark ink-wash dojo, red sun, canvas-drawn vector fighters, procedural particles, WebAudio SFX.
- Duplicate starter card ID removed; 30 cards total, 10 enemies.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created full game files: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `js/data.js`, `js/save.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/render.js`, `js/battle.js`, `js/main.js`.
- Implemented title screen, campaign map, duel intro, battle screen, victory/defeat/ending modals, deck viewer, Dojo upgrades/rest, help modal.
- Implemented complete combat engine, enemy AI/intents, boss phase 2, statuses, posture breaks, card upgrades, save/load, card rewards, level-ups.

- Fixed `card-name` CSS bug (now `display:block`) that caused names to overlap type/art.
- Fixed title seal and title footer positioning; label changed from “Insight” to “Experience” for XP bar.
- Added desktop card-node flex growth and `card.static-card` styles.

### Active
- Visual QA and gameplay balancing after CSS fixes; battle card layout must be re-verified after `card-name` display fix.
- Dojo screenshot after fix (`screenshots/dojo2.png`) shows card names now correctly placed.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Re-test battle screen after card-name CSS fix; check card footer/name/art spacing and bottom clipping.
2. Play through several fights (e.g. Ren, Taro, Mei) to verify balance, enemy intents, posture break, statuses, dodge/counter, defeat/retry.

6. Optionally improve canvas fighter art/background contrast if time permits.

  • Guard absorbs damage and resets at the start of your next turn.
  • Posture recovers each turn. A broken opponent is staggered and skips their action.
  • Balance also matters: if yours breaks, incoming damage rises by 50% for a turn.
  • Bleed drains health at the end of the afflicted fighter's turn.
  • Vulnerable takes +30% damage; Weak deals −25%; Dodge avoids one hit entirely.
  • Counter answers the next attack. Strength adds damage to every hit.
  • Exhaust cards leave the duel after one use. Insight is earned in battle and spent in the Dojo.

limb(ctx,...){
 outline...

Works regardless color. Add.

ctx.fillStyle = shade(color,-8); ellipse...

const ang = Math.atan2(hy-ey,hx-ex);

ctx.fillStyle=skin; beginPath ellipse(1,0,6,4.5); fill; stroke;
